2013, 3969-70 of 2013, 3967-68 of 2013 and transfer case TPC No 19 of
2019) - reg.

Sir,

Attention is drawn towards the judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court dated
28.02.2019, the judgment in the aforesaid cases is abundantly important for the
Organisation. The Hon’ble Supreme Court has considered the appeals where the common
question of law if the special allowances paid by an establishment to its employees would
fall within the expression “basic wages” under Section 2(b)(ii) read with Section 6 of the Act
for computation of deduction towards provident fund. After considering all the appeals, the
Hon’ble Supreme Court has allowed the appeal (Civil Appeal No. 6221 of 2011 )
preferred by the Regional P F Commissioner and finding no merits, has not interfered with
other appeals preferred by establishments .

2. The Hon’ble Court has held that:-

"14, Applying the aforesaid tests to the facts of the present appeals, no
material has been placed by the establishments to demonstrate that the
allowances in question being paid to its employees were either variable or were
linked to any incentive for production resulting in greater output by an employee
and that the allowances in question were not paid across the board to all
employees in a particular category or were being paid especially to those who
avail the opportunity. In order that the amount goes beyond the basic wage, it
has to be shown that the workman concerned had become eligible to get this
extra amount beyond the normal work which he was otherwise required to put
in. there is no data available on record to show what were the norms of work

Sub: Updation of Annual Accounts for the year 2018-2019 — regarding

Madam/Sir,

The Information Services Division is in the process of updation of Annual Accounts centrally
by auto-selection of establishments. In this process, a new option to block the establishment(s)
for processing of annual accounts has also been provided to facilitate the field offices to block any
specific establishment(s) specifying reason(s) therefor.

a, The enhancement has been made in the EPFO Application Software for auto-selection of
establishment(s) and provision to block establishment(s) for Central Processing of Annual
Accounts. To this effect a provision is made available for current year (i.e. 2017-2018), for prior
to current year (i.e. prior to 2017-2018) and next year (2018-2019).

c The option is available with the Dealing Assistant-Accounts to block the establishment(s),
justifying with valid reason(s), for central processing for the next year i.e. 2018-2019 upto March
31%, 2019.

4. In addition, the option to block the establishment(s), justifying the valid reasons, for central
processing for current year (i.e. 2017-2018), for prior to current year (i.e. prior to 2017-2018) has
also been provided to the Dealing Assistant-Accounts upto March 26", 2019 (1730 Hrs). The
central processing of annual accounts has been temporarily suspended from 20.03.2019 to
26.03.2019 (1730 hrs). A report in this regard has already been introduced to monitor the blocked
establishments at the level of DA/SS/APFC.

5. All establishments pending for annual accounts processing for 2017-2018 barring blocked
establishments would be centrally processed from March 26", onwards. All establishments
pertaining to next year i.e. 2018-2019, barring blocked establishments, would centrally be
processed from April 1%, 2019 or the date of Gazette Notification for Interest declaration,
whichever is later. In case, any blocked establishment is to be unblocked later for processing of
annual accounts, facility will be provided shortly.

6. Therefore, all the field offices are requested to identify the establishments to be blocked,
citing valid reasons. Further, as a preparatory activity for processing of annual accounts for the
year 2018-2019, the field offices are further requested to clear all the pending transactions on day
to day basis facilitating smooth and flaw-less central processing of annual accounts.

Subject: Proposals for purchase of ready built office accommodation or land for
construction of office buildings and staff quarters on free-hold / lease-hold
basis

Madam / Sir,

Many of the EPFO Offices are presently functioning out of rental premises and a
substantial amount is being incurred on a recurring basis towards monthly rentals. There
are also places where there is a demand for purchase or construction of staff quarters. It
has been deemed desirable that in respect of all offices that are operating out of rented
premises immediate action should be taken to either purchase ready built accommodation
or land for construction of office buildings. Similarly, actions should also be taken to

purchase ready built staff quarters wherever required,

2. The first priority in attaining the above objective is to ensure that all the Regional
Offices move into self-owned premises in the first instance. In this connection the list of
EPFO Offices indicating whether the respective offices are working out of self-owned
premises or rental premises is enclosed so that concerted and pointed actions can be taken
by the respective Zonal Offices / Regional Offices. The list has been prepared on the basis
of information available on the records of Head Office.

respective Zonal Offices / Regional Offices towards the objective of ensuring that all offices
operate from self-owned buildings / premises:

No. Conf.16(1)2016/Annual Report Dated: 14.03.2019
To,

All Additional CPFC (HQ)s /Additional CPFCs in-charge of Zones,
All Regional PF Commissioners-I in-charge of Regional Offices

Sub: Conduct of Meetings of Regional Committee - reg.

Sir,
Please refer to this office’s letters with no. Conf.16(1)2016/Annual Report/10947 dated

04.09.2018 and no. Conf.16(1)2016/Annual Report/13263 dated 19.09.2017 on the above mentioned
subject.

2 Your attention is invited to paragraph 11 of EPF Scheme, 1952 which provides that "Regional
Committee shall meet at least twice in each financial year". It is the responsibility of the Secretary of
the Regional Committee to ensure that this provision of the Scheme is complied with.

3; It is observed that for most of the Regional Committees, two meetings were not held during
the financial year 2017-18. The fact that for several Regional Committees, two meetings are not held
during the financial year has also been adversely commented on by Audit.

4. Further, it is brought to your notice that even though the term of office of a Regional
Committee is 3 years, according to clause (2B) of para 5 of EPF Scheme, 1952, the members of the
Regional Committee shall continue to hold office until the appointment of their successors is notified
in the Official Gazette. Thus, meetings of Regional Committees can be held even after expiry of the
term of 3 years and not holding meetings on this ground is not a valid explanation.

5. Considering the seriousness of the matter, it may be ensured that at least two meetings of the
Regional Committees are held during the year 2018-19. As the year 2018-19 is ending on 31.03.2019,
it may be ensured that the second meeting of Regional committee, if not held already, may be held
by 31.03.2019.

Yours faithfully,

an PA

(Rajesh Bansal)
Additional Central PF Commissioner HQ (Conference)

Sub: - Compliance of International Workers — reg.

As you are well aware that the substituted Para 2(ja)(b) under Para 83 of the EPF
Scheme defines an International Worker as “an employee other than an Indian employee,
holding other than an Indian Passport, working for an establishment in India to which the
Act applies”.

Subject to provisions of the substituted Para 2(f) and the proviso to Para 2(ja), under
Para 83 of the EPF Scheme, any employee working in an establishment covered under EPF
& MP Act 1952 and holding a foreign Passport is an International Worker.

It has been brought to the notice of this office that the field offices are facing
difficulties in obtaining data of International Workers working in their jurisdiction. Following
the issue, the Head Office has collected data of International Workers from reliable sources.

In order to facilitate compliance in the field offices and ensure effective enforcement
of the Scheme provisions, data of International Workers working in India was sent to all the
Zonal offices on 01.03.2019.

It is requested that compliance must be ensured for all the International Workers
working in India and a monthly progress report in this regard must be sent to the
undersigned by email (acc.hq.caiu@epfindia.gov.in).

Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith a Online RTI Application of Sh. Catta Vikram Rao
received in this office on 30.01.2019. for seeking information under the Right to Information Act. The Copy
of the letter is transferred to you for necessary action under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The
information has to be provided directly to the applicant under intimation to the undersigned. It is certified
that the applicant has deposited the application fee ie. Rs. 10/-

If the desired information does not pertain to the concerned division or some part of information is
held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward /transfer the application or such
Part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s 5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005
respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to
find out as to which division/public authority is concerned with the information even after making
reasonable efforts, in such cases RTI request is to be sent back to Public Information Division, Head Office,
but should not be disposed or kept pending with the CPIO It would, however, be the responsibility of the
CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made reasonable efforts to find out the
particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

If some part of the information concerns to public authority under any State Government or the
Union Territory Administration, the CPIO receiving the application should inform the applicant that the
information may be requested from the concerned State Government/UT Administration. Application, in
such a case, need not be transferred to the State Government/UT Administration.

Name & Address of the Appellate Authority may also be mentioned in the reply, so that the applicant
can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of decision given by the
public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

Sub: - Issue of Certificate of Coverage to members of Social Security Schemes
that are not administered by EPFO.

1. The legislative scope of the Social Security Agreements entered into by
India provides that in relation to India the agreement shall apply to members of all
legislations concerning:

i. Old age and survivor's pension for employed persons;
ii. | Permanent and total disability pension for employed persons

2. As mandated in the Social Security Agreements (SSA’s), EPFO is the
Competent Institution in India to issue Certificate of Coverage to members of various
social security schemes falling within the legislative scope of the SSA’s.

3. The online COC software in place to issue COC’s to the members of EPFO
is based on UAN therefore it does not allow anyone who does not have a UAN to
apply for COC.

4. An online facility for issue of COC to members of social security schemes
other than those administrated by EPFO is yet to be developed.

5. Till the launch of such online facility, the Certificate of Coverage to the
members of Organizations not covered under the EPF & MP Act shall be issued by
the International Workers Unit, EPFO Head Office.

Subject: Allowing members of EPS 95 the benefits of pension on actual salary as per the
orders of: Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in the matter of R.C. Gupta & ors. Vs
RPFC, EPFO & Ors. In SLP No. 33032-33033 of 2015 — regarding.

Sir.

Under the EPF Scheme 1952. contribution on wages higher than the statutory wage

limit is dealt under Para 26(6). As per this Para, for provident fund contribution on higher
wages. joint option of employee and employer is to be submitted and the same is required to
be accepted by EPFO.
ws However, if an employer and employee have contributed under the EPF Scheme,
1952 on wages higher than the statutory wage limit. without joint option of employee &
employer. and the EPF Account of the concerned employee has been updated by EPFO on
the basis of such contribution received, then by action of employee. employer and EPFO, it
can be inferred that joint option of employee and employer has been exercised and accepted
by EPFO. Therefore. in such cases, for implementing the directions issued vide Head Office
Cireular Pension-1/12/33/EPS Amendment/96/Vol.[1/34007 dated 23-03-2017. formal joint
option of employee and employer should not be insisted.
Ff As per the Proviso to Para | 1(3) of EPS. 1995 (as it stood prior to amendment of EPS.
1995 w.e.f, 01-09-2014) joint option of employee and employer was required for remittance
of contribution on wages higher than the statutory wage limit for treating such higher salary
for the purpose of pensionable salary. Therefore. to implement the directions given under
H.O circular dated 23-3-2017. joint option of employee and employer for remitting
contribution under EPS. 1995 on wages higher than the statutory wage limit is required.
However. it has come to the notice of Head Office that in respect of some establishments.
pension contribution on higher wages was already remitted in to the Pension Fund at the
relevant period of contribution prior to 01-09-2014. in such cases joint option of employer
and employee need not be insisted for.

Subject: Installation of Sofar PV panel at Roof Top at the offices of EPFO- reg.
Sir,

REIL is working as expert CPSE and Project Management Consultant (PMC), to undertake
installation of Grid Connected Roof Top Solar (RTS) Project at building/offices of EPFO under
Ministry of Labour & Employment vide MNRE letter No.03/88/2015-16/GCRT dated 31.05.2016.

Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India based on the inputs received from
its CPSEs/Autonomous Bodies/Departments have directed EPFO to approach REIL to take up
installation of Grid Connected Rooftop Solar Power Plants.

Details of sites were handed over to REIL by EPFO & the sites were surveyed by REIL. After
initial assessment, REIL have floated tender for the sites surveyed and sanctioned by MNRE vide
NIT No.REIL/BID/RTS(C)/2018-19/002 dated 25.06.2018. After technical evaluation and reverse
bidding process, the NOAs for solar potential of 1382 KWp under RESCO model have been released
to the respective bidders and the same was communicated to EPFO vide email dated 15.10.2018.
The list of the selected developers with levelized tariff for potential of your site is enclosed herewith
for your ready reference.

Now, the developer selected for your site will approach you for implementation of Solar
Power Plant. The Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) has to be signed between your office and
developer as per MNRE format. The same has been forwarded by REIL and copy of same is being
enclosed herewith. It is worth mentioning here that installation of the solar power plant at sites will
be started only after the signing of this PPA.

The project is developed on RESCO mode. The salient features of the Renewable Energy
Service Company (RESCO) mode is as under:

(a) The roof top solar PV panel project will be executed by the Developer selected by the
Rajasthan Electronic Instrumentation Limited (REIL),

(b) The Developer will invest its own capital and will operate and maintain the project.

(c) EPFO field offices will enter in to Power Purchase (PPA) Agreement with REIL or its
authorised agency (ies) at a mutually agreed tariff on zero lease rental basis for roof top for
predefined period.

Sub: Supply of information under Right to Information Act, 2005 - reg.

Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith a Letter of Advocate Zunaid Khan_ received in this office
on 08.01.2019 for seeking information under the Right to Information Act. The Copy of the letter is
transferred to you for necessary action under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The information has to be
provided directly to the applicant under intimation to the undersigned. It is certified that the applicant has
deposited the application fee ie. Rs. 10/-

If the desired information does not pertain to the concerned division or some part of information is
held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward /transfer the application or such
Part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s 5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005
respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to
find out as to which division/public authority is concerned with the information even after making
reasonable efforts, in such cases RTI request is to be sent back to Public Information Division, Head Office,
but should not be disposed or kept pending with the CPIO It would, however, be the responsibility of the
CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made reasonable efforts to find out the
particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

If some part of the information concerns to public authority under any State Government or the
Union Territory Administration, the CPIO receiving the application should inform the applicant that the
information may be requested from the concerned State Government/UT Administration. Application, in
such a case, need not be transferred to the State Government/UT Administration.

Name & Address of the Appellate Authority may also be mentioned in the reply, so that the applicant
can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of decision given by the

public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.
Yours faithfully,

offices of the EPFO, if so requested by the office concerned;

Attention is invited to Head Office Circular letter +=No. | HRM-
I1/A.10(198)13/803/Vol.1/16380 dated 09.11.2017, vide which it was conveyed that if a Central
Government employee joins another department on the basis of recruitment made by UPSC, his pay
can be protected in the new department and to take appropriate action to protect pay / grant past
service benefit after adopting due procedure to all officers who have joined this Organisatign after
tendering technical resignation from previous Central Government department. As far as grant of
such benefit to those officers who were earlier employed with Central PSUs / State | PSUs/
Universities / Semi Government Institutions / Autonomous Bodies etc. are concemed, jit was
informed that the matter is being taken up with DOP&T and after getting necessary guidelines from
DOP&T, a separate communication shall be issued in this regard.

2. The Ministry of Labour & Employment vide letter No. A-12034/06/2017-SS.I dated
02.11.2018 (copy enclosed) has forwarded a specific clarification of DOP&T obtained by them vide
DOP&T Note No. 1315232/2018-Estt.(Pay-I) (copy enclosed) to be read with UPSC’s letter No.
1/292(21)2010/R-IV/SPC-II dated 04.10.2018 (copy enclosed). The DOP&T has clarified | in the
above said note that “protection of pay is available to the candidates coming from PSUs/ Banks etc
only if the selection of such candidates in Government is through UPSC and is through interview and
not through an open competitive examination. However. in order to differentiate the two methods o
selection ie. Selection on direct recruitment basis through ‘Open competitive Examinatiok and
selection on direct recruitment basis through ‘Interview’ in_cases where the appointment
Government servant is through UPSC and where ‘Open competition’ is followed by ‘Interview "
Subsequent to this, the matter was taken up with UPSC by the Ministry of Labour & Employment
with request to convey the method adopted in the direct recruitment process of Assistant Provident
Fund Commissioners in this Organisation. In response to this, UPSC has sent a reply to M inigtry of
Labour & Employment vide letter No. 1/292(21)2010/R-IV/SPC-II dated 04.10.2018 in which it has
been clarified that recruitment to 253 3 posts of APFC 2012, the written and interview marks were
accorded 50:50 weightage whereas in the latter case (170 posts of APFC 2016
interview marks were accorded 75:25 weightage in the final result. Subsequently, Ministry of
Labour & Employment vide letter No. A-12034/06/2017-SS I dated 02.11.2018 has forward
clarification of DOP&T vide DOP&T Note No. 1315232/2018-Estt.(Pay-I) to be read with UPSC’s

Subject: Annual Account Data Rectification.
Madam/Sir,

Many references have been received by NDC regarding missing contribution especially for October 2016
(October paid in November) to February 2017 (Feb paid in March) and Annual accounts for the Year 2016
already issued.

To address this issue, a new two level functionality “Annual Accounts Data Rectification (Account Year
2016 Issued)” has been provided in Field office application. This functionality enables to fetch missing
contribution for the establishments where annual accounts have been processed for 2016-17.

e Inthe functionality the DA accounts inputs the TRRN number having missing contribution.

e After running though validation checks a detailed screen is shown, showing the TRRN details along
with buttons to generate PDF report of missing contribution and saving the TRRN.

e The PDF shows the TRRN details along with the member id’s that are already present and member
ids that are getting added.

e Onsaving the task flows to AC Accounts level. On submission by AC accounts the mismatch in the
TRRN is removed.

Since, contributions are getting added through this functionality, it is mandatory to verify the details in
PDF with original source documents at DA and APFC level. After approval of APFC the contribution is
posted in the relevant tables of backlog accounting, so it is mandatory to check the Form3a Check list
backlog. Any local adjustment made for the contribution of the member using Annexure E / VDR etc.
may be checked for correctness.

Sir,

Attention is invited to Head Office circular No.HRM-I/Misc./2017/26043 dated
11.01.2017 on the subject cited above advising all the officers & staff to desist from bringing political
or other outside influence for furthering their interests either by themselves or by their family
members.

2. However, it is seen that large number of representations are still being received from
employees of Central Board of Trustees, EPF which are directly sent to public representatives like
Members of Parliament, Hon’ble Ministers and other dignitaries. In some cases, it is seen that family
members of the employees send their requests for transfer/posting and grievance related to service
matters directly to public representatives.

3. It is reiterated that Rule 20 of CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 which is mutatis mutandis
applicable to the employees of Central Board of Trustees, EPF by virtue of Regulation 18 of EPF
(Officers? and Employees’ Conditions of Service) Regulations, 2008, stipulates that no government
servant shall bring or attempt to bring any political or outside influence to further their interest in
respect of service matters like transfer & posting.

4. Therefore, all the officers & staff are advised to desist from bringing political or other
outside influence for furthering their interests either by themselves or by their family members, as
bringing outside influence in such matters are violation of Conduct Rules and entails disciplinary

action as per rules.

Subject: Para 68HH: Non-refundable advance to a member in case of

Ref. No.: MOL&E Notification No. G.S.R.1182(E)dated 6" December 2018.
Sir/Madam,

Please find enclosed a copy of the above said notification issued by
Ministry of Labour & Employment. The said notification shall come into force from
the date of its publication in the official gazette.

The newly inserted paragraph 68HH shall enable a member who is no
longer in employment for a month, to avail upto 75% of the total provident fund
standing to his credit. Further, since the membership would be retained, it would
enable a member to avail pensionary benefits at the time of retirement. The
advance is non-refundable.

Kindly take note that the newly notified paragraph 68 HH shall be, in
addition to, the existing paragraph 69(2) of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme,
1952 The said paragraph 69(2) enables a member to withdraw the full amount
standing to his credit in the provident fund on ceasing to be an employee in any
establishment for a continuous period of two months immediately preceding the
date on which he makes an application for withdrawal. The requirement of two
months waiting period shall not, however, apply in cases of female members
resigning from the services of the establishment for the purpose of getting married.

Subject: Workshop for Representatives of Exempted Establishments to be held from

Regarding.

Sir,

Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security has been conducting
Workshop for the Exempted Establishments on Employees’ Provident Fund and
Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952 for the last several years. The response for the programme
from the industry has been quite encouraging and almost all of the participants felt that such
programmes should be conducted regularly to inform the developments in EPF and EPS
Administration.

Keeping in view the recent developments in EPF and EPS Administration, the Academy
has designed a two-day Workshop for Representatives of Exempted Establishments on
31° January to 01° February, 2019,

During the workshop following issues will be discussed:

Discussing the provisions of the Act and the Schemes.

Deliberating on key issues posing challenges in compliance.

Explain the conditions of granting Exemption.

Describe Books/Records and Returns to be maintained/filed by Exempted Establishments
Investment pattern for provident funds.

Duties and Responsibilities of the Role of Exempted Establishments

Employer’s responsibilities in respect of International Workers.

Computerization in EPFO.

2. The above workshop is for the Senior/Middle Level Management of the Exempted
Establishments in their establishments. It is requested to sponsor suitable level officers from
exempted establishments covered under your jurisdiction for the above said Workshop.

3. The participation fee for residential participants is Rs. 5,000/- (Rupees Five thousand
only) per participant including both boarding and lodging and Rs. 4,000/- (Rupees
Four Thousand only) per participant for Non- Residential participants. Fee once
deposited shall not be refunded after acceptance of nominations by the Academy.
However, 90% fee is refundable in case of only those nominations which are not accepted by the

Academy due to any reason. There are only limited seats available for the nominations. Hence,
the nominations shall be accepted on “First come First Serve” basis. Nominations will be
confirmed only after confirmation of receipt of fee at PDNASS.

Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith RTI application 02.11.2018 under RTI Act of Sh. P. Gopal
Shastry received in Pension Section on 19.11.2018 through PID Section for seeking information
under the Right to Information Act. The copy of the letter is transferred to you for necessary action
under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The information has to be provided directly to the
applicant under intimation to the undersigned.

If the desired information does not pertain to the concerned division or some part of
information is held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward/transfer
the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s
5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such
transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/public authority is
concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

Name & address of the Appellate Authority may also be mentioned in the reply, so that the
applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of
decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

In this context please refer the order of the full bench of CIC in Appeal No.
CIC/AT/A/2008/01280, dated 29.09.2008 between Sri Ketan Kantilal Modi Vs. Central
Board of Excise & Customs wherein it is held as under:-

“In case CPIO, CBEC transfers appellant’s RTI application electronically to the
subordinate Commissionerates, the latter shall process these information requests as
independent requests under Section 6({1) and collect from the petitioner all requisite
fees including the application fee as if the application were made independently by him
to that public authority subordinate to the CBEC.”

Sub: - (a) Competent Authorities to decide on issues related to
cancellation/modification/extension of Certificate of Coverage issued by EPFO field
Offices.

(b) Nodal officer for coordination with the Competent
Authorities/Institutions of the foreign countries with which India has Social Security
Agreement.

It has come to the notice of this office that Certificates of Coverage (Detachment
Certificates) are being issued by the field offices for period beyond the period stipulated
in the respective Social Security Agreement (SSA).

A Certificate of Coverage (COC) should be issued through the routine procedure in
cases where the period of detachment of the employee is within the period of
detachment given in the SSA. However beyond this period a COC can be issued only
with the consent of the Competent Authority/Institution of the country with which India
has entered into an Agreement on Social Security.

The standard procedure for issue of COC beyond the period stipulated in the SSA will
be as shown below:

e A joint application (from the employee and the employer) for extension of COC
beyond the period stipulated in the SSA has to be submitted in the concerned
Regional Office of EPFO under the jurisdiction of which the establishment falls.

e The application has to be forwarded to Head Office by the concerned Regional
Office with their recommendation based on the provisions of the SSA that India is
having with the country, where the applicant is going to work.

e RPFC-I (IWU), Head Office, shall forward the request to the Competent
Institutions/Authority of the SSA country.

e After receipt of the consent of the Competent Institution/Authority of the SSA
country the same will be communicated to the concerned Regional Office
following which COC can be issued beyond the period stipulated in the SSA.

Sub.: Supply of Information under RTI Act —2005-reg.
Sir,
Please find enclosed herewith an online RTI application 21.10.2018 under RTI Act of Sh. Siju
Jose T received in Pension Section on 23.10.2018 through Nodal Officer for seeking information
under the Right to Information Act. The copy of the Jetter is transferred to you for necessary action

under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The information has to be provided directly to the
applicant under intimation to the undersigned.

If the desired information does not pertain to the concerned division or some part of
information is held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward/transfer
the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s
5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such
transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/public authority is
concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

Name & address of the Appellate Authority may also be mentioned in the reply, so that the
applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of
decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

In this context please refer the order of the full bench of CIC in Appeal No.
CIC/AT/A/2008/01280, dated 29.09.2008 between Sri Ketan Kantilal Modi Vs. Central
Board of Excise & Customs wherein it is held as under:- +

“In case CPIO, CBEC transfers appellant’s RTI application electronically to the
subordinate Commissionerates, the latter shall process these information requests as
independent requests under Section 6(1) and collect from the petitioner all requisite
fees including the application fee as if the application were made independently by him
to that public authority subordinate to the CBEC."”

No copy is required to be endorsed to Head Office for information

Sub.: Supply of Information under RTI Act ~2005-reg.
Sir,

If the desired information does not pertain to the concerned division or some part of information is held
by other division or public authori , the concerned CPIO shall forward/transfer the application or such part of
it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s 5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005
respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such transfer, However, if the CPIO is not able to
find out as to which division/public authority is concerned with the information even after making reasonable
efforts to find out the concerned division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It
would, however, be the responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that
he made reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

Name & address of the Appellate Authority may also be mentioned in the reply, so that the applicant
can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of decision given by the
public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

In this context please refer the order of the full bench of CIC in Appeal No.
CIC/AT/A/2008/01280, dated 29.09.2008 between Sri Ketan Kantilal Modi Vs. Central Board of
Excise & Customs wherein it is held as under:-

“In case CPIO, CBEC transfers appellant's RTI application electronically to the subordinate
Commissionerates, the latter shall process these iriformation requests as independent requests
under Section 6(1) and collect from the petitioner all requisite fees including the application fee
as if the application were made independently by him to that public authority subordinate to the
CBEC,”

Yours faithfully,

information is held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward/transfer
the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s
5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such
transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/public authority is
concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of
decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

Board of Excise & Customs wherein it is held as under:-

subordinate Commissionerates, the latter shall process these information requests as
independent requests under Section 6(1) and collect from the petitioner all requisite
fees including the application fee as if the application were made independently by him
to that public authority subordinate to the CBEC.”

Sub:- Land mark Central Government Industrial Tribunal Judgment against
condonation of delay - reg. .
Sir,

A Copy of land mark Judgment in the matter of Sarwan Singh Dhiman and sons
Vs Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, Chandigarh (EPF No. 02/2017) passed by the
Presiding Officer, Central Government Industrial Tribunal-Cum-Labour Court -1
Chandigarh has been forwarded to this office by e-mail byRPFC-I & ACC( addl charge)
Chandigarh. The copy of complete judgment is being circulated as it may be quite useful
for reference in similar cases pending before various CGIT’s and other courts.

The order made by CGIT-I, Chandigarh disposed of the application filed by the
appellant for condonation of delay in filing appeal before the CGIT. It is alleged by the
appellant that the impugned order dated 24.8.2016 under section 7A of EPF&MP
Act,1952 has not been received by him, but the Ld. Tribunal has stated that there is
nothing on record to show that impugned order was not conveyed to the appellant as
required by law. Vide its order dated 25.07.2017 the Ld. CGIT stated that

“ It is clear from the ratio of law laid down in the above authorities that
when limitation is provided under special law the question of condonation of
delay has to be considered within the parameters contained in the said special
law. The Courts cannot be import into the Act or Rule their discretion so as to
defeat the very purpose of such special enactment. Resultantly, this Tribunal
does not have powers to condone the delay beyond the period of 120 days as
mentioned in Rule 7(2) of the Rules. As sequel of above discussion, it is held
that appeal filed by the appellant herein is hopelessly time barred as such the
delay in filing the appeal is uncondonable in view of the embargo contained in
Rule 7(2) of the Rules. Accordingly the application is rejected.”

urs’ faithfully,

information is held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward/transfer
the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s
5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such
transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/public authority is
concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

Name & address of the Appeilate Authority may also be mentioned in the reply, so that the
applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of
decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

Board of Excise & Customs wherein itis held as under:- ,

subordinate Commissionerates, the latter shall process these information requests as
independent requests under Section 6(1) and collect from the petitioner all requisite

to that public authority subordinate to the CBEC.”

Please find enclosed herewith RTI application 13.06.2018 under RTI Act of Sh. U.M.Meshram

the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s
5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such
transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/pubiic authority is
concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of
decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

Board of Excise & Customs wherein it is held as under: -

Sir,

Your attention is invited to paragraph 11 of EPF Scheme, 1952 which provides that "Regional
Committee shall meet at least twice in each financial year". It is the responsibility of the Secretary of
the Regional Committee to ensure that this provision of the Scheme is complied with.

2. A list showing the number of meetings of each Regional Committee held during the year,
2017-18 is enclosed herewith. It is observed that for most of the Regional Committees, two meetings
were not held during the financial year 2017-18. The fact that for several Regional Committees, two
meetings are not held during the financial year has also been pointed out by Audit.

2. Further, it is brought to your notice that even though the term of office of a Regional
Committee is 3 years, according to para 5 of EPF Scheme, 1952, the members of the Regional
Committee shall continue to hold office until the appointment of their successors is notified in the
Official Gazette. Thus, meetings of Regional Committees can be held even after expiry of the term of
3 years and not holding meetings on this ground is not a valid explanation.

4. Considering the seriousness of the matter, it may be ensured that at least two meetings
of the Regional Committees are held during the year 2018-19.

concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made

especially those belonging to the above mentioned three states.

generation of UAN without Aadhaar for employees resident in any of the three states

Sub: Strengthening and streamlining of the Nidhi Aapke Nikat
platform — Regarding.

Sir/Madam,

The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation touches lives of millions
in the country everyday. It is almost a lifetime relationship between EPFO
and its subscribers. Over the past years, EPFO has successfully adopted
several reforms to improve its public delivery of social security benefits.
However, the vast magnitude of stakeholders with their ever rising
expectations under rapidly changing technological scenario necessitates a
very responsive and transparent grievance management system which
addresses the issues and concerns of its stakeholders in a meaningful and
substantive manner.

Z. It is observed that on the one hand we have a large category of
subscribers and stakeholders who are well versed in using technology based
platforms such as CPGRAMS, EPFIGMS, emails etc. to voice their concern,
while on the other, there is also a sizeable number of stakeholders for
whom using technology-based platform for registering their grievances may
be difficult. Therefore, there is a need to reach out all stake holders
including those who may not be cormfortable to use the above technology
based platforms in case of difficulty/grievance.

a, One of the ways to deal with above situation is to use the programme
like Nidhi Aapke Nikat as a medium of public interface which was initiated
with the very purpose of being more accessible to its stakeholders including
employers, to redress their grievances, and to sensitize all the stakeholders
about the new initiatives undertaken in their interest by the Organisation,

4, In the view of above, it is felt necessary to issue guidelines afresh for
streamlining Nidhi Aapke Nikat programme and strengthening the grievance
redressal mechanism through such programme. Therefore, the following
instructions are issued:

5(4) and 6(3) of the RT1 Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such

concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made

applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of

Sub. : Operationalisation of Concurrent Audit in EPFO- Instructions regarding
Sir,

Concurrent Audit Cell (CAC) has been set up recently in EPFO, situated at NDC. The present
objective is to study the key transactions involved in settlement of claims at the time of happening or
parallel with the transaction, on daily basis to facilitate field offices in timely detection and prevention of
financial frauds.

The following reports are generated through Concurrent Settlement Report:-
A) Claim under progress in which DoB/Name has been Changed

B) Claim under progress from Inoperative Account.

C) Multiple payments to the same bank Account.

D) Claim under progress of High value.

The observations based on the above reports are emailed to the respective offices directly by
CAC on the day of generation of the report. However, it has been observed that only few offices are
responding to the e-mails forwarded by CAC, while majority of the replies only state that nothing
adverse has been found or no irregularities has been detected. However, physical verification of records in
some offices has revealed that the issues raised by Concurrent Audit has either been overlooked or
casually dealt with. This defeats the very purpose of Concurrent Audit Cell. Non-submission of timely
replies by the concerned offices has been viewed seriously by the Competent Authority.

It is requested that the e-mails of CAC have to be scrutinized thoroughly and in case any
discrepancies found, the reply may be sent along with the necessary documents and action taken report.

Yours faithfully,

for the proper discharge of his duties. Sub-Section (5) further provides that any
officer whose assistance has been sought shall render all assistance to the Central

contravention of the provisions of the Act, such other officer shall be treated as
Central Public Information Officer” and may be liable for penalties under Section 20

functions of another public authority.

the public authority, to which such application is made, shall transfer the application
or such part of it as may be appropriate to that other public authority and inform the
applicant immediately about such transfer”.

The Head Office is in receipt of various proposals from different divisions

Guidelines for Procurement of Goods and Services are laid out under Rule 142
to Rule 206 of GFR.

The Rule 149.Govt. e- Marketplace (GeM) has made it mandatory for
procurement of Goods and Services by the Ministries/Departments that are
available on GeM. All procuring offices are to strictly follow the conditions laid
out in Rule 149 (i) to Rule 149(viii) of the GFR on GeM.

However in order to bring more transparency and best price discovery
of the Goods & Services being procured by the office, it is important that the
information in regards to procurement process should be widely publicized,
as laid out under GFR Rule159 E-Publishing. This information should also be
compulsorily uploaded in the tenders section of the EPFO website including
the ones being processed through Gel, in order to give wide publicity so as

to ensure healthy competition for best price discovery.

responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

Subject: Deployment of Leave module in HRSoft — regarding
Madam/Sir,

In pursuit of making EPFO a paperless organization, the existing leave module covering
Casual Leave and Restricted Holiday in HRSoft has been extended to include Earned Leave,
Half Pay Leave, Extra Ordinary Leave, Child Care Leave, Paternity Leave and Maternity Leave
thereby replacing the existing system of physical forms. This facility is available as “Online Leave
Apply” option under transaction mode in the HRSoft home screen of individual officers and staff.
A detailed step-wise explanation of the leave application process along with screen shots is
attached herewith for ready reference.

2. All officers and staff are mandatorily required to apply for the above mentioned category
of leave through the HR Soft module and paper based leave applications will not be accepted
and processed henceforth for the leave types mentioned above. EOL, Commuted Leave (on
medical grounds, etc.) and other leave types not covered above would continue to be made on
paper forms till functionalities for them are made available.

3. All controlling/leave Sanctioning authorities must assure that they have the authority
before sanctioning/rejecting the leave application sent to them for approval. All officers/staff
should proceed on leave only after their leave is sanctioned by the approving authority.

concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, howéver, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particutars of the concerned division/public authority.

Subject: Erroneous transfer settlement by Field Offices-Regarding.

Sir,

An analysis of erroneous transfer settlements by field offices reveals that the same are being

handled in field offices in a very casual manner. This is leading to lot of avoidable grievance.

2. In the circumstances, the following may be strictly ensured by field offices for streamlining

the transfer claims:

® Itis the responsibility of the transfer-out office to satisfy themselves about the details
of the member ID to which the amount and service is to be transferred.

» Member Details of all member ids across India are already made available under FO
Interface under Unified Portal and the same is to be used to verify and satisfy before
initiating and approving the transfer using “Verify member Details” functionality.

» ‘The exemption status of the establishment to which the transfer is being made should
also be checked before approving the transfer, since if the establishment is exempted,
the PF amount has to be sent to the trust and not to transfer-in Office.

» It should be ensured that the need for rejection of the amount at the transfer-in office

does not arise.

specified medical emergency and major illness like cancer, heart surgery etc. as specified from
time to time. The objective behind providing the said assistance from the EPF Staff Welfare
Fund is to mitigate hardships faced by the individual. Therefore, the fact that the individual is

Sub: Wrongly seeded aadhaar no - Introduction of new functionality regarding
Sir,

Various mails have been received from field offices reporting the rejection
of DLCs due to incorrect Aadhaar number seeded against PPOs through DLC
registration of the pensioners. After examining the issue, a new functionality
‘Rectify Mismatch Aadhaar number has been provided in the application
software. The scenario of the case is explained below:-

If pensioner submits his DLC using PPO number which does not pertain
to that pensioner and the same PPO is available in our data, in such cases the
details of Name , Date of birth and Account No. will get mismatched with the
available data. In this situation, the task will be pushed to field offices through
‘Manual Confirmation of Jeevan Pramaan’ function. However, If DA/SS(PDS)
wrongly approved such mismatch cases, the Aadhaar no. will get seeded
against wrong PPO No and the life certificate flag will get enabled.

In the aforesaid situation, if the original pensioner submits his Digital life
certificate, the application software will reject the DLC by throwing rejection
status as ‘Already seeded Aadhaar number does not match with currently received
Aadhaar no.’

This function will facilitate to remove such incorrect Aadhaar numbers in
the pensioner database populated against wrong PPO number and it will
inactivate the life certificate flag also. A letter will also get generated against the
original pensioner requesting him/her to submit the DLC once again.User
manual in this regard was already circulated to all field offices through mail
dated. 28.05.2018. :

Field offices are requested to utilize this function in order to remove the
incorrect aadhaar number so that the pensioner could submit his/her DLC
without rejection,

Yours faithfully.

1952. Para 4 of the said notification states as under —

"Proceeds arising out of exercise of put option, tenure or asset switch or trade of any asset

Para 5 of the said notification states as under —

"Turn over ratio (the value of securities traded in the year/average value of the portfolio at the
beginning of the year and at the end of the year) should not exceed two.”

stipulates the following :-

"The exempted establishment shall intimate to the RPFC concerned the details of depository
Participants (approved by the Reserve Bank of India and Central Government), with whom and
in whose safe custody, the investments made in the name of trust, viz., Investments made in
securities, bonds, etc. have been lodged. However, the Board of Trustees may raise such
sum or sums of money as may be required for meeting obligatory expenses such as
settlement of claims, grant of advances as per rules and transfer of member's P.F.
accumulations in the events of his/her leaving service of the employer and any other
receipts by sale of the securities or other investments standing in the name of the
Fund subject to the prior approval of the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner.”

4. Para 4 and 5 allows the Trusts of the exempted establishments to invest/re-invest the
funds received through maturity proceeds, asset switch or trade of any asset before maturity
etc. subject to conditions laid under Para 4 and 5 of the notification. Whereas, condition no. 20
of Appendix — ‘A’ to Para 27AA of the EPF Scheme, 1952 prescribes for prior approval of Regional
P.F. Commissioner for selling of the securities for meeting obligatory expenses such as
settlement of claims and grant of advances etc. Itis therefore clarified that the Trust of

Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith an online RTI application 16.05.2018 under RTI Act of Sh.
Prakritish Sen Eshore received in Pension Section on 14.05.2018 for seeking information under the
Right to Information Act. The copy of the letter is transferred to you for necessary action under the

information is held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward/transfer
the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s
5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such
transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/public authority is
concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of
decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

CIC/AT/A/2008/01280, dated 29.09.2008 between Sri Ketan Kantilal Modi Vs. Central
Board of Excise & Customs wherein it is held as under:-

“In case CPIO, CBEC transfers appellant's RTI application electronically to the
subordinate Commissionerates, the latter shall process these information requests as
independent requests under Section 6(1) and collect from the petitioner all requisite
fees including the application fee as if the application were made independently by him
to that public authority subordinate to the CBEC.”

Railways— Reg.

Sir/Madam,

In the last meeting with representatives of the Railways held on
09.05.2018 in Head Office, it has been decided that in order to effectively
monitor the progress in uploading contract details by various user and Sub-
user offices of the Railways for the purpose of coverage of contract employees
engaged, Zonal ACCs should have monthly interaction with Divisional Railway
Managers of the DRM Offices located in the same city. If the DRM Office is not
located there, RC/OIC of the Regional Office concerned will have monthly
meetings with the DRM Office located in their respective areas.

Zonal ACCs/RC/OICs should maintain good liaison with the DRMs and
make every effort to impress upon them to ensure social security to all
contract/casual employees working with them.

Zonal ACCs/RCs/OICs will prepare the reports of the monthly meetings
and forward a copy to CAIU, Head Office routinely.

Further, all Zonal ACCs and RCs/OICs will not only have to monitor the
progress in uploading of contract details by the Railways in the Principal
Employer Portal but also have to ensure verification of such uploaded details in
respect of their offices and subsequent action taken wherever necessary for
enrolment of all eligible employees promptly & routinely.

Sub.: Supply of Information under RTI Act —2005-reg.
Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith an online RTI application 12.05.2018 under RTI Act of Sh.
Parveen Kohli received in Pension Section for seeking information under the Right to Information
Act. The copy of the letter is transferred to you for necessary action under the Right to Information
Act, 2005, The information has to be provided directly to the applicant under intimation to the
undersigned.

If the desired information does not pertain to the concerned division or some part of
information is held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward/transfer
the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s
5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such
transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/public authority is
concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

Name & address of the Appellate Authority may also be mentioned in the reply, so that the
applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of
decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

In this context please refer the order of the full bench of CIC in Appeal No.
CIC/AT/A/2008/01280, dated 29.09.2008 between Sri Ketan Kantilal Modi Vs. Central
Board of Excise & Customs wherein it is held as under:-

“In case CPIO, CBEC transfers appellant’s RTI application electronically to the
subordinate Commissionerates, the latter shall process these information requests as
independent requests under Section 6(1) and collect from the petitioner all requisite
fees including the application fee as if the application were made independently by him
to that public authority subordinate to the CBEC.”

Yours faithfully,

other establishments in the form of consolidated instructions as mentioned below:-

referring/seeking permission for inspection from CAIU, Head Office :

1000 as per Wage Analysis Report on CAIU Portal.

(e) Establishments during currency of enquiries under section 7A of the Act.

(f) Exempted establishments not filing monthly returns.

Madam/Sir,

Annual Performance Assessment Report (APAR) for the year 2016-17 in respect of
officers in the cadres of Addl. CPFC, RPFC and APFC was submitted through SPARROW
Software. Now, APAR for the year 2017-18 in respect of the aforesaid grades are to be
submitted through SPARROW.

2. It has been further decided that from the reporting year 2017-18, APAR in respect of
other cadres has also to be generated online through SPARROW portal for which necessary
infrastructure is being deployed. A separate circular in this regard shall be issued in due
course. Therefore, keeping this decision in view, no APAR in paper-based format in
respect of any cadre/post may be printed, generated or circulated.

s. As regards APAR for the year 2017-18 in respect of the cadres of Addi. CPFC, RPFC
and APFC as in the previous year, the following are to be carried out in a time bound
manner:-

(i) Workflow to determine movement of APAR: Workflow in SPARROW in respect of
each officer may be created by the office where he/she is posted viz. ZO, RO,
ASD-HO or PDNASS. There may be single Workflow for the whole year or multiple
Workflows for each broken periods depending on the posting of the officer during the
assessment year under various Reporting/Reviewing Authorities. To simplify the
procedure, it has been decided that Reviewing and Accepting Authorities in all
Workflows shall be the same officer. Utmost care must be taken in selecting
Reporting and Reviewing Authorities in the Workflow and it is advised that names of
such Authorities may be obtained in advance from the records of work assignment in
the present/previous office(s).

(ii) Generation of APAR with Part-I: Immediately after creation of Workflow, all offices
viz. ZO, RO, ASD-HO and PDNASS must generate APAR with Part-l(Personal Data)
thereof duly filled in respect of each officer so that the same is sent to their
SPARROW Inbox for submission of self-resume by them.

Sub.: Supply of Information under RTI Act ~2005-reg.
Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith an on line RTI application 27.03.2018 under RTI Act of Sh.
Rama Ranjan Mohanty received in Pension Section for seeking information under the Right to
Information Act. The copy of the letter is transferred to you for necessary action under the Right to

Information Act, 2005. The information has to be provided directly to the applicant under intimation
to the undersigned.

If the desired information does not pertain to the concerned division or some part of
information is held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward/transfer
the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s
5(4) and 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such
transfer. However, if the CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/public authority is
concerned with the information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned
division/public authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however, be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he made
reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public authority.

Name & address of the Appellate Authority may also be mentioned in the reply, so that the
applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of
decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

In this context please refer the order of the full bench of CIC in Appeal No.
CIC/AT/A/2008/01280, dated 29.09.2008 between Sri Ketan Kantilal Modi Vs. Central
Board of Excise & Customs wherein it is held as under:-

“In case CPIO, CBEC transfers appelilant’s RTI application electronically to the
subordinate Commissionerates, the latter shall process these information requests as
independent requests under Section 6(1} and collect from the petitioner all requisite
fees including the application fee as if the application were made independently by him
to that public authority subordinate to the CBEC.”

Yours faithfully,

Sub:- Wage analysis report in CAIU dashboard - regarding.

Sir,

As you are aware it is very important that Non-Contribution Period i.e. NCP days are
correctly reflected in ECR to ensure that non-contributory period does not get counted as
contributory period. Also, it is important to ensure that the employers especially contractors,
fully contribute towards provident fund for the full working period of an employee and not on
very low unrealistic wages.

2. In order to provide a tool to the Zonal ACCs and OICs for monitoring the above issues,
wage analysis report will now be provided in the CAIU dashboard. Zonal ACCs and OICs can see
the analysis of wages in respect of their Zones / RO and ensure that wherever required, the
verification of ECR details may be done to ensure that there is correct reporting of NCP days
and full compliance in respect of individual employees.

3, The report will provide establishment wise and members wise details in a particular wage
slab. Accordingly, the OICs may immediately start verifying details in respect of members
where the Zero wages have been reported. Thereafter, the next slab can be taken up for
verification and so on. For verification of cases other than those listed on the dashboard,
permission be taken from CAIU, Head Office.

4. Establishments where abnormally high number of employees is shown to have Zero
wages or very low un-realistic wages, may be got inspected. Evasion if any may be detected,
assessed and recovered at the earliest.

5. No separate report need be sent on action taken by Zonal ACCs and OICs to Head Office.
The performance of Zonal ACCs and OICs shall be measured in Head Office by comparing the
wage analysis summary reports of successive months. Zonal ACCs may also review the
performance of ROs accordingly.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: - Application of Syed Mohamed for seeking Information Under RTI Act,

Please find enclosed herewith a copy of online RTI application dated 09.03.2018 of
Sh. Syed Mohamed seeking information under RTI Act.

2. Whereas on scrutiny of the application (copy enclosed) it is found that the information
sought by applicant regarding point No. B “regarding amount of revised pension,
differential amount deposited, pension revision arrears disbursed” and Point
No. C (8) “Total number of pensioners who submitted fresh joint option for
higher contribution during the period 01.09.2014 to 28.02.2015 and 01.03.2015
to 31.08.2015 is related to all field offices.

3. Therefore, in accordance with Section 6(3) of RTI Act, 2005 the application is hereby
transferred to all field offices for supply of information on point No. B “regarding
amount of revised pension, differential amount deposited, pension revision
arrears disbursed” and Point No. C (8) “Total number of pensioners who
submitted fresh joint option for higher contribution during the period
01.09.2014 to 28.02.2015 and 01.03.2015 to 31.08.2015 directly to the applicant
under intimation to the undersigned.

4. It may be mentioned that if the desired information does not pertain to the
concerned division or public authority or some part of information is held by other
division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward/transfer the application or
such part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s 6(3) of
the RTI Act, 2005 and inform the applicant immediately/about such transfer. However, if
the CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/public authority is concerned with the
information even after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned division/public
authority to which the application could be transferred. It would, however be the
responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made against his decision, to establish that he
made reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the concerned division/public
authority.

5. The Name and Address of the Appellate Authority may also be mentioned in the
reply, so that the applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such
period or from the receipt of decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by
the decision.

6. This may please be treated as most urgent.
Yours faithfully,

Madam/Sir,

Further to the instructions issued vide reference number
NDC/Appl.Software/2018/30094 dated 16-03-2018, wherein directions were given to make use
of the reports provided on the settlement of online claims to step up the vigil, the following
further instructions are issued for strict compliance:-

(i) Out of the list of online claims being provided, atleast 1% of online cases must be
test checked for genuineness.

(ii) The member/employer may also be contacted, if felt necessary based on the above
observations, to confirm genuineness of the claim.

(iii) | Since the employer is being provided with the list of online claims preferred by the
members from his establishment through email, the employer may be advised to
scrutinise the same regularly and inform irregularity, if any, detected by them.

(iv) The list of online claims verified as mentioned at (i) above, shall be recorded and
reported to ACC (Zone) with due observations on regular basis.

(v) In case any software related issue is identified while processing the claim which
needs to be addressed for improving the robustness of the system, the same may be
raised with ACC (IS) for rectification.

(vi) In case of detection of any fraud or any suspicious transaction, the instructions on
Fraud Analysis and Management be followed.

Yours faithfully,
